name: Béroul
bio: Béroul is the name given in the manuscript to the author of one of the two great Old French verse romances of Tristan and Iseut. He is otherwise unknown: he names himself twice in the text and appears to have written in the second half of the twelfth century, probably in western France, in the Anglo-Norman or Norman-influenced French of that time.

His poem survives in a single damaged manuscript (BnF fr. 2171) that lacks both its beginning and its end, about 4,485 lines of octosyllabic couplets in all. It belongs to the so-called common version of the legend, rougher and more dramatic than Thomas's courtly version, and tells of the lovers' life in the forest, their repeated deceptions of King Mark, the ordeal of the oath and their eventual reconciliation with the king.
